# SHELDON ### Reasoning through Dual Search over Hypothesis and Observation Spaces [Harshit Joshi](https://harshitjoshi.com)\*  ·  Priyank Shethia\*  ·  [Monica S. Lam](https://suif.stanford.edu/~lam) Stanford University  ·  \*equal contribution
[![arXiv](https://img.shields.io/badge/arXiv-2610.18025-b31b1b.svg)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.18025) [![Paper](https://img.shields.io/badge/Paper-PDF-blue.svg)](https://sheldon.genie.stanford.edu/sheldon.pdf) [![Project page](https://img.shields.io/badge/Project-page-8A2BE2.svg)](https://sheldon.genie.stanford.edu) [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-green.svg)](LICENSE) [![Python 3.12](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.12-3776AB.svg)](pyproject.toml)
(a) SHELDON searches a hypothesis space and an observation space jointly; edges in the hypothesis space are refinements. (b) New hypotheses drive improvements on a system-optimization task. (c) Scores on DiagnosisArena, ORCA-Bench, ARC-AGI-2, and QNN circuit topology.

## Abstract Test-time scaling has enabled large language models to solve increasingly complex reasoning, discovery, and optimization tasks, but existing approaches often suffer from fixed search strategies, or hypothesis-centric reasoning that under-explores informative evidence. Inspired by the hypothetico-deductive method and dual-space models of scientific discovery, we introduce SHELDON, a scientific reasoning harness that jointly models hypothesis and observation spaces. By treating observations as first-class objects, SHELDON can identify gaps in its current understanding, uncover new hypotheses, and design investigations that better distinguish among alternatives. Across diagnosis, abstract reasoning, and optimization benchmarks, SHELDON outperforms evaluated baselines by up to 26.7 points. On system root cause analysis tasks, SHELDON discovers 29.8 percentage points more ground-truth causes and investigates 34.4 percentage points more of the discovered causes than other baselines, demonstrating that joint hypothesis-observation search leads to broader and more effective scientific reasoning at test time.
## Results All methods use GPT-5.6-terra with high reasoning effort; SHELDON delegates code implementation to GPT-5.6-luna. Best score per column in **bold**. ### Diagnosis, root-cause analysis, abstract reasoning, circuit discovery | Method | Family | DiagnosisArena | ORCA-Bench | ARC-AGI-2 | QNN topology | |:--|:--|--:|--:|--:|--:| | ReAct | Reasoning agent | 72.00 | 40.00 | 25.00 | 0.80 | | Codex | Coding agent | 76.00 | 40.00 | 24.44 | 0.82 | | EvoX | Meta-evolution | — | — | 47.50 | 0.85 | | RLM | Recursive agent | 78.00 | 40.00 | 15.00 | 0.48 | | GoS | Reasoning agent | 68.00 | 30.00 | — | — | | **SHELDON** | Scientific reasoning | **84.00** | **66.67** | **59.17** | **1.00** | ### Molecular optimization (DOCKSTRING) Best molecule each method docked within 1,000 docking calls, per protein target. *Library best* is the top of the 260k-compound DOCKSTRING database. | Method | ADRB1 | CDK2 | PPARA | PPARG | F2 | PGR | |:--|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:| | Codex | 5.97 | 6.92 | 7.46 | 6.38 | 9.31 | 7.40 | | ReAct | 8.49 | 8.32 | 8.98 | 8.40 | 7.79 | 7.67 | | EvoX | 8.63 | 7.19 | 8.62 | 7.41 | 8.36 | 9.17 | | CORAL | 11.01 | 9.32 | 9.64 | **9.69** | 9.10 | **10.65** | | **SHELDON** | **11.26** | **10.26** | **9.85** | 9.47 | **9.85** | 9.99 | | *Library best* | *11.33* | *9.53* | *9.91* | *9.53* | *9.31* | *9.74* | ### System optimization (ADRS) Mean / best over three runs per method on the same hardware. Higher is better except Cloudcast, where the score is a cost. *Human best* is the task's published reference solution. | Method | EPLB | PRISM | Cloudcast ↓ | Txn scheduling | LLM-SQL | |:--|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:| | Codex | **0.1441** / **0.1441** | 25.60 / 25.65 | 677.10 / 618.10 | 3069 / 3558 | 0.6877 / 0.7109 | | ReAct | 0.1440 / 0.1440 | 26.24 / **26.26** | 621.11 / 618.10 | 3932 / 4000 | 0.7001 / 0.7069 | | EvoX | 0.1318 / 0.1433 | **26.26** / **26.26** | 618.10 / 618.08 | 4009 / 4184 | 0.7149 / 0.7196 | | ScientistOne | 0.1319 / 0.1440 | **26.26** / **26.26** | 624.10 / 618.10 | 2533 / 3962 | 0.7034 / 0.7137 | | Arbor | 0.1433 / 0.1435 | 26.25 / **26.26** | 618.80 / 618.10 | 3668 / 3759 | 0.7130 / 0.7218 | | CORAL | 0.1436 / 0.1436 | **26.26** / **26.26** | 619.00 / 619.00 | 4077 / 4201 | 0.7115 / 0.7163 | | **SHELDON** | **0.1441** / **0.1441** | **26.26** / **26.26** | **618.09** / **618.07** | **4198** / **4274** | **0.7204** / **0.7245** | | *Human best* | *— / 0.1265* | *— / 21.89* | *— / 626.24* | *— / 2724.8* | *— / 0.6920* | ### Ablations | Variant | DiagnosisArena | ORCA-Bench | ARC-AGI-2 | QNN topology | |:--|--:|--:|--:|--:| | **SHELDON (full)** | **84.00** | **66.67** | **59.17** | **1.00** | | without comparative analysis | 78.00 | 56.67 | 50.00 | 0.883 | | without observation space | 70.00 | 53.33 | 50.00 | 0.867 | | without continued exploration | 82.00 | 53.33 | 57.70 | 0.733 | Removing the observation space costs the most, and most consistently. Full tables, per-task costs, and the coverage analysis are in the [paper](https://sheldon.genie.stanford.edu/sheldon.pdf).
## Getting started ### Install ```bash git clone https://github.com/stanford-oval/sheldon.git cd sheldon make setup # uv venv + editable install cp .env.example .env # fill in one provider ``` `.env` takes either an OpenAI-compatible endpoint (`OPENAI_BASE_URL`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`) or `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`. Model names are whatever your endpoint serves; set `model:` in `configs/default.yaml` or pass `--model`. Check the install without an API key: ```bash make smoke # the full pipeline, offline, against a scripted model sheldon ls # registered benchmarks, methods and engines sheldon check # which benchmark data is present ``` ### Run The method is registered as `sheldon`. A first run on ARC-AGI-2: ```bash scripts/fetch_arc.sh sheldon run -b arc-agi-2 -m sheldon -n 10 --tag pilot sheldon report ``` ### Configs A run is described by a YAML config. `configs/default.yaml` is the baseline; an experiment config extends it and overrides what it changes, and `configs/experiments/` holds the ones behind the tables above: ```bash sheldon run -c configs/experiments/087_arc_agi_2_sheldon_session.yaml sheldon run -c configs/experiments/087_dockstring_sheldon_terra.yaml sheldon run -c configs/experiments/082_skydiscover_llm_sql_sheldon_terra.yaml ``` A config has four parts. Everything in the first three is hashed into the run id, so a changed setting is a different run; the execution block is not. ```yaml extends: ../default.yaml # what: the cell benchmark: arc-agi-2 split: eval # or a benchmark-specific split, listed in its module's `splits` limit: 20 # tasks per cell; null = the whole split seed: 0 # subsample seed, so every method sees the same tasks method: sheldon # sheldon | direct | best-of-n # how: the model and the engine engine: toolloop # toolloop | simple | react | codex | rlm provider: auto # auto | openai | anthropic model: gpt-5.6-terra effort: high # low | medium | high | xhigh | max max_tokens: 16000 thinking: true # how much: per-task budget; the loop stops at whichever binds first max_rounds: 4 # null lifts a cap max_calls: 40 max_usd: 1.0 max_seconds: null # execution: changes speed, never the numbers concurrency: 8 # tasks in flight cache: true # model calls cached on disk resume: true # finished tasks are skipped on re-run tag: exp087 notes: one line for the report params: # method knobs; see the table below mode: session rounds: 6 ``` Every field can be set from the command line, which wins over the file: `--model`, `--effort`, `--engine`, `--rounds`, `--max-usd`, `--max-calls`, `--task `, `--tag`, `--no-cache`. A method parameter is `-p key=value` with a JSON value, nested with dots: ```bash sheldon run -c configs/experiments/087_arc_agi_2_sheldon_session.yaml \ --model gpt-5.6-luna --max-usd 4 \ -p mode=staged -p select_k=3 -p benchmark_opts.isolate=true sheldon run -c ... --dry-run # print the resolved config and exit ``` ### Hyperparameters The method's knobs live under `params:`. Defaults are the code's; the ones the experiment configs change most are at the top. | Parameter | Default | What it does | |:--|:--|:--| | `mode` | `staged` | `staged` asks each stage in a fresh call over freshly rendered state; `session` runs a round's deciding stages as turns of one conversation (needs a native tool-loop engine) | | `rounds` | `6` | rounds per task, within `max_rounds` | | `n_initial` | `5` | hypotheses explore opens with in round 1 | | `n_explore` | `3` | hypotheses explore adds in each later round | | `select_k` | `5` | hypotheses tested per round; kept ones take no slot | | `max_regions` | `10` | regions per space (hypothesis map and observation map each); when a map is full, a merge call before explore asks the model which regions to fold together, and the merged region keeps its history. `0` lifts the cap | | `set_aside_cooldown` | `3` | rounds a shelved hypothesis waits before explore may revive it | | `stagnation_rounds` | `2` | rounds without a new best score or observation before the whole shelf unlocks | | `plan` | `true` | one call before round 1 separates the problem from the specification of the answer | | `candidate_analysis_max_evals` | `3` | evaluator runs per hypothesis per round, on benchmarks with a scoring function | | `candidate_analysis_patience` | `2` | measured iterations in a row that fail to improve before the local loop stops | | `candidate_analysis_min_gain_pct` | `0.5` | the improvement, in percent of the seed's score, that counts as progress | | `candidate_analysis_concurrent` | `true` | run a round's local loops at once | | `candidate_analysis_engine` | the run's engine | the engine that builds and tests artifacts, with its own `candidate_analysis_engine_params` | | `stage_probes` | `true` | let the deciding stages search before deciding; `_probes` overrides one | | `_probe_calls` | explore `8`, select `2`, candidate_analysis `12`, comparative_analysis `10`, exploit `4`, finalize `6` | tool-call ceiling for one call of that stage | | `probes` | `[web_search, web_fetch, run_shell]` | the generic tools every stage can reach, beside the benchmark's own; `[]` leaves only the benchmark's | | `benchmark_opts` | `{}` | per-benchmark switches, such as `isolate`, `max_evaluations`, `max_docking_calls` | | `offer_tools` | per benchmark | whether an engine that brings its own tools is also offered ours | `direct` and `best-of-n` take `n` (default `5`) and `test_rule`, and nothing else. ### Engines An engine is how one "ask the model, let it act" step runs. The benchmark decides which tools exist and the method decides the strategy; the engine is the piece you swap to change what executes a step, without touching either. `sheldon ls` lists them. | Engine | What it is | When to use it | |:--|:--|:--| | `toolloop` | the provider's native tool-calling loop (default) | any endpoint with tool support; every call is cached and budgeted | | `simple` | one completion, tools ignored | the no-tools ablation, or an endpoint with no tool support | | `react` | Thought / Action / Observation as text, parsed by the harness | a proxy that mangles tool schemas, or a paper's ReAct baseline | | `codex` | the Codex CLI as the step, with our probes served to it over MCP | a coding agent in the loop; needs `codex` on `PATH` | | `rlm` | a Recursive Language Model: a REPL the model programs, with sub-calls on its own context | the RLM baseline; needs the `rlm` package in the venv | Pick one with `engine:` in the config or `--engine` on the command line, and tune it under `params.engine_params`: ```yaml engine: codex params: engine_params: mode: research # research: workspace-write, network, web search; reason: read-only reasoning: high # defaults to the run's `effort` timeout: 2400 # seconds per codex call isolate: true # run under bubblewrap, like the benchmark's own shell cwd: scratch/codex-work usd_watchdog: true # kill a call at the remaining budget; codex is told the limit serve_probes: true # false: codex with nothing but its own tools ``` ```yaml engine: rlm params: engine_params: max_iterations: 8 max_depth: 1 timeout: 1500 isolate: true rates: [2.50, 15.00] # $/M tokens in, out: the endpoint returns no price ``` `toolloop` and `react` take `max_steps` (default `4`), the tool calls per step before the model is asked to answer; `toolloop` also takes `model`, which puts that engine on a model of its own. **Two engines per run.** The deciding stages and the stage that builds and tests artifacts can run on different engines. This is how the results above were produced: the stages that explore, select and revise run on `toolloop` with the run's model, and the local build-and-test loop runs on a second engine or a cheaper model. ```yaml engine: toolloop model: gpt-5.6-terra params: candidate_analysis_engine: codex # or toolloop with another model candidate_analysis_engine_params: reasoning: high timeout: 2400 isolate: true ``` ```yaml params: candidate_analysis_engine: toolloop candidate_analysis_engine_params: model: gpt-5.6-luna ``` **Comparing engines honestly.** `codex` and `rlm` bring their own shell and file access on top of whatever the harness offers, and their model calls do not pass through the harness's cache, so a run on either is not comparable to one on `toolloop` and gets its own row. `probes: []` with the benchmark's `isolate` is the usual setting for both. ### Benchmarks | Name | Task | Get the data | |:--|:--|:--| | `med-dx` | DiagnosisArena: diagnose a patient by asking for history, examination, labs and imaging | `scripts/prepare_med_dx.py` | | `orca-bench` | ORCA-Bench: find the root cause of a production incident | `scripts/prepare_orca_bench.py` | | `arc-agi-1`, `arc-agi-2` | induce a grid rule from worked examples | `scripts/fetch_arc.sh` | | `skydiscover` | rewrite a program so an evaluator scores it higher: the ADRS systems tasks and QNN circuit topology | `scripts/prepare_skydiscover.py --download --datasets` | | `dockstring` | design a molecule that binds a protein target and stays drug-like | `uv pip install ".[dockstring]"` then `scripts/prepare_dockstring.py --download` | Data lives under `data//`, or wherever `SHELDON_DATA` points. ### Read a run Each run writes `runs/________/` with its config, predictions, scores and a full trace per task. ```bash sheldon report # the table: scores, then what they cost sheldon failures # the worst tasks, with trace paths sheldon show # one trace, rendered top to bottom sheldon ui --open # every run and trace, with the hypothesis state per task sheldon log --serve # every model call, prompt and reply in full ``` Model calls are cached on disk and runs resume, so re-running a config costs nothing for work already done.
Repository layout
``` sheldon/ core/ types, config, budget, LLM + cache, trace, sandbox, isolation benchmarks/ one module per benchmark; base.py is the contract methods/ sheldon/ (the method and its prompts), stage.py engines/ how one model step runs: toolloop, simple, react, codex, rlm runner.py async execution, resume, artifacts ui/ the trace console and the model-call log cli.py ls / check / smoke / run / report / show / ui / log / failures configs/ default.yaml and experiments/ scripts/ fetch and prepare benchmark data, re-score finished runs ```
> **Caution.** The Python sandbox and shell execute model-written code in a > subprocess with a timeout. That is isolation, not a security boundary. Set > `benchmark_opts.isolate: true` to run commands under bubblewrap where a > benchmark supports it.
